findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout; a hanging add/save/delete leaves the button on 'Saving…' forever
findings.where: Plant detail page journal form / JournalEntryItem / Journal page (useApiClient, useApiFetch)
findings.steps: Open /plants/2, make POST /api/journal hang (never respond), type an entry and click Add entry, wait more than 10 s.
findings.expected: Request aborts after 10 s with a visible error; button becomes usable again, typed text kept.
findings.actual: After 13 s the button still reads 'Saving…' and is disabled; no error ever appears.
findings.evidence: Playwright: {btn:'Saving…', disabled:true} 13 s after click with a hanging route. No timeout option in useApiClient/useApiFetch.

findings.title: Non-JSON 200 response on the Journal page is shown as a list of blank entries ('18 entries match')
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal return 200 with Content-Type text/html and body '<html>proxy</html>' (e.g. a proxy/login page), then type in the search box.
findings.expected: An error state saying the journal could not be loaded, with a retry.
findings.actual: The page says '18 entries match' (the length of the HTML string) and renders 18 cards that show only '–'. A response with null plant_name/body/entry_on also shows a blank card with '–'.
findings.evidence:
main text: '18 entries match

–

–...'. The response is never checked to be an array.

findings.title: Journal load errors have no retry button (Journal page and plant detail journal)
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal?* return 500/503, then open Journal from the nav, or open a plant from the Plants list.
findings.expected: Error message with a Retry button that reloads the data without a page reload.
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown, with no button. On /journal the only way back is to change the search text; on the plant page you have to reload. Meanwhile the plant page badge still says '2 entries' next to the error.
findings.evidence: /journal main text: 'Could not load the journal.'; buttons in main: []. Plant detail section: '2 entries … Could not load the journal.' and no retry control.

findings.title: Entry length is counted in UTF-16 units on the client but in characters on the server: emoji entries are capped at 250, and longer valid entries can't be edited
findings.steps: 1) In the New entry box paste 300 emoji ('🌱'). 2) Create a 500-emoji entry through the API (the server accepts it with 201), then click Edit and Save on the plant page.
findings.expected: Up to 500 characters allowed no matter which script is used; an entry the server accepted can be edited and saved.
findings.actual: 1) The textarea stops at 250 emoji and says '0 characters left'. 2) The edit form says '-500 characters left' and Save is refused with 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.'
findings.evidence: Playwright: typedCodepoints 250, hint '0 characters left'; edit hint '-500 characters left', alert 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.' maxlength and .length count UTF-16 code units; pydantic max_length counts code points.

findings.title: Out-of-range ids give 500 Internal Server Error on the journal endpoints
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite OverflowError on integers above 64 bits).
findings.evidence: curl: 'Internal Server Error 500' for all four calls; plant_id 99999999999999999999 also gives 500.

findings.title: Retrying a timed-out or failed add creates a duplicate entry (no idempotency)
findings.where: POST /api/journal from the plant detail page
findings.steps: Add an entry while the response gets lost (the server commits but the client sees a network error or timeout), then click Add entry again.
findings.actual: The form keeps the text and shows an error. A second click sends a new POST with no idempotency key, so the server inserts a second, identical entry.
findings.evidence: addEntry() posts with no request key, and create_entry inserts with no dedupe check.

findings.title: Long plant names make the Journal page scroll sideways at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a plant named 'SupercalifragilisticSupercalifragilisticSupercalifragilistic', add a journal entry to it, set the viewport to 375 px and open /journal.
findings.expected: No horizontal scrolling; the plant name wraps.
findings.actual: document scrollWidth is 522 px. The .journal-feed__plant link has no overflow-wrap, so the card and the date stick out past the viewport.
findings.evidence: scrollWidth 522; elements overflowing: journal-feed__item card, journal-entry__head, journal-entry__date.

findings.title: Search longer than 80 characters shows a raw validation message instead of results
findings.steps: Type or paste 81 characters into Search.
findings.expected: The input is limited to 80 characters (maxlength), or a friendly message is shown.
findings.actual: The list is replaced by 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'. The input has no maxlength.
findings.evidence: main text ends with 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'.

findings.title: Server-local 'today' check can reject today's entry for users in other time zones
findings.steps: As a user whose local date is ahead of the server's (e.g. UTC+10 in the morning, server on UTC), add an entry dated today. The form defaults to today.
findings.actual: Server returns 422 'Journal date cannot be in the future.' because it compares with date.today() on the server, while the client's max/default use the browser's local date.
findings.evidence: schemas.py uses date.today(); utils/format.ts todayIso() uses the browser's local time.

findings.title: Deleting or editing an entry that is already gone leaves the stale entry on the page
findings.steps: Open a plant in two tabs, delete an entry in tab A, then click Delete (or Edit then Save) on the same entry in tab B.
findings.expected: The list refreshes and the entry disappears. A repeat delete counts as done.
findings.actual: Tab B shows 'Journal entry not found.' and the deleted entry stays in the list until the page is reloaded; the list is not refreshed on error.
findings.evidence: removeEntry/save only refresh on success; DELETE returns 404 for missing ids.

findings.title: Dates like year 0001 are accepted
findings.expected: Implausible dates are refused with a visible reason.
findings.actual: 201 Created; the entry is listed as the oldest, dated '1 Jan 1'.
findings.evidence: curl returned 201 with entry_on 0001-01-01 (test entry deleted afterwards).
